note: Story video for Dispatch No. 030, drawn only from its verified caption and Spec Sheet. Photos, all U.S. government works at NARA, unrestricted: Rushmore in July 1939 with scaffolding over Roosevelt's head (Public Roads Administration 30-N-40-2431, NARA 135804230); Washington completed, Jefferson in progress, September 1935 (South Dakota Projects, NARA 5604020); Mount Rushmore National Monument, May 1939 (NARA 5604046); Washington's head above the rubble, Forest Service photo (95-GP-340-344861, NARA 7004388); Mount Rushmore Memorial practically finished, June 1942 (NARA 5604049); the finished carving (NPS 79-MORU-294, NARA 404575438, dated 1952). No film of the work ending in October 1941 was found at NARA, so this is a Story Card. The 8 a.m. dispatch that day (No. 029, Reuben James) has only two public domain photos, too few for a Story Card.

segments.say: For fourteen years, nearly four hundred workers rode down a granite cliff on steel cables to carve it with dynamite. Not one of them died.
segments.caption: For fourteen years, nearly 400 workers rode down a granite cliff on steel cables to carve it with dynamite. Not one of them died.

segments.say: October thirty first, nineteen forty one. Work on Mount Rushmore comes to an end.
segments.caption: 31 October 1941. Work on Mount Rushmore comes to an end.

segments.say: It had begun in October, nineteen twenty seven.
segments.caption: It had begun in October 1927.

segments.say: About ninety percent of the carving was done with dynamite, blasting until only inches of rock were left.
segments.caption: About 90 percent of the carving was done with dynamite, blasting until only inches of rock were left.

segments.say: Workers climbed seven hundred stairs to the top each morning, then were lowered over the face in bosun chairs.
segments.caption: Workers climbed 700 stairs to the top each morning, then were lowered over the face in bosun chairs.

segments.say: One remembered the pay as eight dollars a day.
segments.caption: One remembered the pay as $8 a day.

segments.say: Gutzon Borglum, the sculptor who designed it, had died that March.
segments.caption: Gutzon Borglum, the sculptor who designed it, had died that March.

segments.say: His son, Lincoln Borglum, carried the job to its finish.
segments.caption: His son, Lincoln Borglum, carried the job to its finish.

segments.say: Each head is about sixty feet tall.
segments.caption: Each head is about 60 feet tall.

segments.say: Five weeks later came Pearl Harbor.
segments.caption: Five weeks later came Pearl Harbor.
